issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: the problem UML and the template Main show/assume single-argument constructors that take only the animal's name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")), but the solution implements Animal and all concrete animals with two-argument constructors (String name, int age). This inconsistency will confuse students about which constructor signature to implement and will cause their code (following the template/problem) to be incompatible with the solution's structure or the example usages in Main.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signatures consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement UML and the template Main to show that Animal and concrete animals include an 'age' attribute and require constructors (String name, int age), or (B) modify the solution to use single-argument constructors (String name) and remove the extra 'age' parameter so it matches the UML and template usage.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch: the problem UML and description specify that Animal has a single attribute 'name', but the solution's Animal class introduces an additional 'age' attribute. This structural difference changes the required constructors and the responsibilities of the Animal class, and is not documented in the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal attributes with the problem specification. Either remove the 'age' field from the solution's Animal class (and its constructor/getters/setters) so Animal only has 'name' as in the UML, or update the problem statement and UML to include the 'age' attribute and indicate that constructors should initialize both name and age.

issues.description: Constructor/attribute mismatch for Animal subclasses: the problem statement and template imply animals have a single attribute 'name' and the example Main uses single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). However, the solution introduces an additional attribute 'age' in Animal and requires two-argument constructors (String name, int age) for Animal and all subclasses. This divergence in constructor signatures/parameters creates confusion for students mapping the UML/problem description and template examples to the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor/attribute model consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Remove the extra 'age' attribute from the solution's Animal class and change subclasses to single-argument constructors (String name) so they match the UML/problem/template; or (B) Update the problem statement, UML, and template Main examples to include the 'age' attribute and show two-argument constructors (String name, int age). Ensure constructor signatures for Seal, Pig, and Goat match the declared attributes in Animal across all artifacts.
